summary: All three round-1 issues are resolved correctly. The vault_* migration is clean and removes every sops.* reference from the Phase 7.5 block. ConditionPathIsMountPoint= is present in the template and verified by the post-render assert. The handler probe/restart split is functionally correct. One informational note on handler ordering: both probe and restart listen on the same event name, which works because Ansible fires handlers in definition order — this is correct but worth a comment to prevent future reordering.

T3-1.verified: deploy.yml Phase 7.5 now uses vault_blogger_telegram_bot_token, vault_blogger_telegram_channel, vault_blogger_prompts_topic_id, vault_publish_callback_hmac_secrets, vault_publish_mode, vault_publish_auto_mode_token, vault_publish_min_score, vault_publish_approval_timeout_min, vault_telegram_forum_chat_id — zero sops.* references remain. Sensitive vars (bot token, HMAC secrets, repo refs) deliberately have no | default() fallback, consistent with the fail-loud strategy and the role's preflight asserts.

T3-2.verified: content-publisher.service.j2 line 13 now has ConditionPathIsMountPoint={{ content_publisher_volume_mount }}. The post-render grep in tasks/main.yml updated to '^(RequiresMountsFor|ConditionPathIsMountPoint|LimitCORE|ProtectSystem|NoNewPrivileges)=' and the assert block extended with "'ConditionPathIsMountPoint=' in cp_unit_grep.stdout". Comment in the template accurately explains the RequiresMountsFor vs ConditionPathIsMountPoint distinction.

T3-3.verified: handlers/main.yml now has two entries listening on 'Restart content-publisher': (1) Probe task that calls ansible.builtin.systemd to read unit state and registers cp_unit_state; (2) Restart task conditioned on cp_unit_state.status.ActiveState | default('inactive') == 'active'. Ansible fires handlers in definition order, so probe runs before restart — the condition is evaluated with the correct value. Wave 1 inactive service: probe returns inactive, restart is skipped (no fail-loop). Wave 2 running service: probe returns active, restart fires.

bonus_improvements.title: Preflight asserts for bot token, HMAC secret, and auto-mode token
bonus_improvements.description: Three assert tasks added at the top of tasks/main.yml guard against empty or too-short values reaching the env-file render. Token >= 30 chars catches empty/placeholder; HMAC >= 64 chars enforces the openssl rand -hex 32 minimum; auto-mode token >= 64 chars only when publish_mode == 'auto'. These are good additions that make the fail-loud strategy concrete at deploy time rather than waiting for a runtime 401 or a silent '' == '' comparison.

bonus_improvements.title: Quoted token values in blogger.env.j2
bonus_improvements.description: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_CHANNEL, CALLBACK_HMAC_SECRETS, and PUBLISH_AUTO_MODE_TOKEN are now quoted. Comment explains the defense-in-depth rationale (word-splitting on hypothetical future format). Correct and matches Task 1's template pattern.

bonus_improvements.title: TASK 7 TODO comment for EnvironmentFile= leading dash
bonus_improvements.description: The TODO correctly identifies that the leading `-` should be dropped when the unit goes active (Task 7). This is a helpful handoff note for Task 7's implementer.

informational_notes.title: Handler ordering relies on definition order — add a comment to prevent accidental reordering
informational_notes.description: The 'Probe whether content-publisher is currently active' handler has `listen: Restart content-publisher`, and the 'Restart content-publisher' handler is triggered by its name matching the notification. Ansible fires handlers in the order they are defined in the file, so the probe runs before the restart — this is correct. However, there is no comment explaining this ordering dependency. A future contributor who swaps the two handler blocks would silently break the guard (restart fires before cp_unit_state is populated, condition evaluates against undefined).
informational_notes.recommendation: Add a one-line comment before the Restart task: '# Must run AFTER the Probe handler above (Ansible fires handlers in definition order).' No code change required.
